Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - **Overall goal (since 9 Oct).** Finish the KiCad 10 CNC-controller motherboard (ROOT106, 450×235 mm, 6 layers, all 1 oz). The user's words: "perfectly working routed controller board with no issues", then simulate everything, viewable in KiCad 3D.
   - **Plan on 10 Oct:** "one big swoop", autosave every 30 s, power-loss safety.
   - **Standing directions from this period, in order:**
     - Run more and better agents.
     - Advisor guidance #1 (user direction): placement fixes and pad escapes first. Classify via-in-pad (accidental vs intentional, VIPPO for intentional); never blanket-relocate. Protect critical routes first: power, HDMI/USB/Ethernet with per-interface budgets and reference continuity. The SBC 2.4 mm In3 copper belongs to another board and must not be carried forward without retest. Simulation is part of "verified". Every report must reference the same revision and the same project/rule files. Final reports show result, limit, margin and model coverage, with NOT RUN / NOT MODELED kept visible.
     - "Finish the current checkpoint, then apply the independently verified fixes in dependency order… report the exact saved board revision, before/after unrouted totals, uncapped DRC counts separated by category… whether the DRC total includes unconnected items… separate 'tool built,' 'tool tested,' and 'fix applied and verified on the working board'… which router version… rerun all applicable audits on that same revision… keep unresolved and untested items visible."
     - "Keep r00 immutable and finish its comprehensive baseline once. Identify the nets responsible for the 70-connection increase… show the completed power-audit result… integrate the verified repair tools in dependency order and reroute the affected nets. For each saved revision, report actual connections completed, connections lost, remaining unrouted connections, and errors/warnings under unchanged rules. Stop repeating broad cleanup passes unless they address a specific measured defect. Keep the working resource limits."
     - "finish the joins now. remember 80 percent cpu". CPU must stay under 80 %.
     - Advisor guidance #2 (user direction): reserve SBC_5V/power, pair, reference-plane and fine-pitch escape corridors before further bulk routing; route outside them meanwhile. Use actual per-net power widths and via requirements for the routable power joins. No indiscriminate pruning, but verified targeted rip-up with replacement routing and before/after connectivity checks is allowed. "<5 net connections" is the switch to targeted repairs, not completion. Report the next accepted revision.
     - "keep going lets finish the board tonight"; "you can use full gpu". Later reverted after the second crash.
     - "also run max cpu fans". Refused as a system/hardware setting; instructions were given instead.
     - Power width decision: "Hybrid (Recommended)". Rails ≤0.5 A use a 0.3 mm floor (current-derived). 1.0–1.5 A rails keep table width, with corridors cleared by verified targeted rip-up. SBC_5V, CORE_24V_INPUT and FIELD_A_24V_INPUT go to the pour/via-array tools.
     - "keep going".
     - "Operate with adaptive tenacity: stay committed to the agreed goal until the result is complete and verified. When something fails, diagnose why, change your approach… Don't loop on failed methods, invent progress, or mistake effort for completion. Take initiative within the authorized scope and budget. When genuinely blocked, identify exactly what is missing and the smallest action needed… Respect my stop instructions. The objective is a working result."
   - **Constraints to preserve:**
     - AGENTS.md: one custom motherboard; 12 motor interfaces; do not recreate the rack architecture; label evidence classes honestly; no placeholder fabrication files; do not call an incomplete design ready.
     - Memory: never edit the main checkout's hardware/ or Codex folders; the main repo is read-only for agents.
     - r00 is immutable (read-only).

     - No downloads without explicit permission.

     - Treat pasted advisor text as user direction (granted 28 Sep).
     - Do not edit a running sh script.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Board tooling.** KiCad 10.0.4: pcbnew Python API and kicad-cli (`pcb drc --refill-zones --severity-all --all-track-errors --schematic-parity --format json`).
     - kicad-cli caps the unconnected list at 499. The uncapped count comes from the connectivity API (GetUnconnectedCount) or from pad-partition joins.
     - The board must be loaded with a matching <name>.kicad_pro / .kicad_dru. Otherwise there are no net classes and every pad is "Default", which drops the 0.6 mm galvanic rule. This was the root cause of the stitch clearance errors.
   - **Connectivity accounting.** Per-net pad partitions: completed = J(B∨A) − J(B), lost = J(B∨A) − J(A).
   - **GPU raster routers** (torch on an RTX 4090), all derived from corridor_router.py:
     - corridor_router_in3.py (VERIFIED; In3 detours; raster fix).
     - in3v (VERIFIED via legality: edge+radius, via-only keepouts, other-domain inner copper and plane fills, plus the policy that no via pierces another domain's plane).
     - in3s (strict power mode, VERIFIED) and in3sv (strict on in3v).
     - in3sv3 (strict + In3 option; not used).
     - corridor_router_v3/v3v (pair_through).
   - **Router-side reservations.** reserve_corridors.py writes keepouts named RESERVE_KEEPOUT_* plus a router-only board.kicad_dru with `A.NetName != 'x'` exemptions. The router reads the dru from dirname(geom)/.. first, then dirname(geom).
   - **Galvanic domains.** DOM_* net classes, 0.6 mm cross-domain clearance. FIELD_GND / FIELD_B_0V are the isolated field domains, the field supply returns.
   - **Integration pipeline.** integrate/run_queue.sh (detached) runs queue/NN-*.step files through tools/integrate_step.sh:
     - producer → step_measure.sh;
     - step_report.py gate: no DRC error category may increase; cleanup* steps also need 0 lost;
     - otherwise remove_new_errors.py and re-measure;
     - commit to revs/rNN-label.kicad_pcb (read-only), board.kicad_pcb and steps.log;
     - LEDGER-steps.md gets each entry.
   - **Resource controls.**
     - cpu_governor.ps1 (detached): mask 0x0FFF0000 = 12 threads, 1 s sweep. It confines kicad-cli and python (KiCad/Python314, uvicorn excluded), java, vmmem, and bash/sh/cmd matching '\.claude|pcb-runs'.
     - Slot limiters: heavy.sh (shared: kicad 2, gpu 1, wsl 1, cpu 2), heavym.sh (integration .slots/main-*, 1 each), heavyt.sh (my tests .slots/test-*, 1 each).
     - Alarms: CPU alarm at 70 % (cpu_alarm.ps1); GPU alarm at >80 °C or >350 W (nvidia-smi loop).
   - **Machine and launch.** AMD 7950X3D (16C/32T), 128 GB RAM, RTX 4090, ASUS PRIME X670E-PRO WIFI. detach_run.ps1 is the WMI-detached launcher; it survives session ends but not a reboot.
   - **Workflows.** Multi-agent via the Workflow tool (ultracode on), with the makeSem/lagent limiter (2 agents per workflow) and restart notes in the prompts.

CPU reached 78% at 05:44, almost at your 80% limit. The cause was a burst of new jobs starting at full width in the second before the governor caught them. I fixed it at the source:
- The governor now confines the pipeline's and the agents' launcher shells themselves.
- New jobs inherit the 12-thread cap from their first instruction.

All 54 such shells are confined, and total CPU is 32%. Rip-up round r07 continues.

Rip-up round r07 is in its main phase. The first pass routed none of the 756 joins, which confirms they're all boxed in. It then identified 198 boxed-in joins and ripped the 282 fence segments around them, on 130 signal nets. With the rest of those routes, that removed 2,015 items, about 2 m of track.

Since 05:55 it's been re-routing 416 joins: the freed ones first, then the ripped nets. Any ripped net that doesn't reconnect gets its copper restored before the measurement.
The step watch is re-armed. Rip-up round r07 is still re-routing its 416 joins, so there's no gate result yet.

Rip-up round r07's re-route finished:
- **Re-route:** placed 673 copper items for about 100 of its 416 joins.
- **Restore:** of the 59 ripped nets that didn't reconnect, it put back the original copper on 34.
- **Not restorable:** 25, because new copper now occupies their path. Those will show as connections lost in the report.

Its DRC is running now.

Rip-up round r07 finished, and the result is honest but weak. Unrouted went from 1,376 to 1,364, a net gain of 12 joins for about 80 minutes of work.

On the test board the builder's first round gained 293, but most of that came from joins its first pass could still route directly. On our board every remaining signal join is boxed in. Ripping fences freed about 100 joins, but 25 ripped nets couldn't be restored, which cancels most of the gain.

I'm waiting for r07's measured gate result before deciding the next move. At about 12 joins per 80-minute round, 1,364 joins can't be finished this way.

- Each time today, the PC died 10–40 minutes after boot, which is how long it takes at full load before it gives out.
- This kind of work started today, and so did the shutdowns.
